IS : 4162 (Part 3 >- 1985 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR GRADUATED PIPETTES 

PART 3 PIPETTES FOR WHICH A WAITING TIME OF 
15s IS SPECIFIED 

(First Revision) 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 3 ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by the 
Indian Standards Institution on 30 October 1985, after the draft finalized 
by the Laboratoryware and Related Apparatus Sectional Committee 
had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 

0.2 This standard was originally published as IS : 4162-1967*. Sub- 
sequently International Organization for Standardization brought out the 
following Standards: 

ISO : 835/M981 Laboratory glassware — Graduated pipettes: 
Fart 1 General requirements 

ISO : 83S/2-1981 Laboratory glassware — Graduated pipettes: 
Part 2 Pipettes for which no waiting time is 
specified 

ISO : 835/3-1981 Laboratory glassware — Graduated pipettes: 
Part \ Pipettes for which a waiting time of 15s 
is specified 

ISO : 835/4-1981 Laboratory glassware — Graduated pipettes: 
Part 4 Blow-out pipettes. 

The Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard 
decided to revise IS: 4162-1967* to align this standard with the above ISO 
standards. Accordingly this standard is now being revised in four parts: 
Part 1 General requirements; Part 2 Pipettes for which no waiting time is 
specified; Part 3 Pipettes for which a waiting time of 15s is specified; and 
Part 4 Blow-out pipettes. 

0.3 In this revision the following have been included: 

a) Method of setting of meniscus, 

b) Procedure for measurement of capacity, 



^Specification for graduated pipettes. 



IS:4162(Part3)-1985 

c) 0*5 ml capacity pipettes with Class A accuracy for type 4 only» 

d) Pipettes for which a waiting time of 15s has been specified, 

e) Pipettes — known as blow-out pipettes» and 

f) Table for dimensions has been modified to bring in line with ISO 
Standards. 

0.4 This standard contains 13*2 which calls for agreement between the 
purchaser and the supplier. 

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of 
this standard is complied with, the final values, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS : 2-1960'^. The number of significant places retained in 
the rounded off values should be the same as that of the specified values 
in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

U This standard ( Part 3 ) specifies the requirements for graduated 
pipettes with comparatively large jets, for which waiting time of 15s is 
specified in order to compensate for the possible effect of shorter delivery 
time, and which are suitable for general laboratory purposes. They are 
adjusted to Class A accuracy. 

1.1.1 The requirements specified are in conformity with IS : 8729-1977t. 

1.1.2 The requirements specified in Part 1 of this standard shall apply. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard definitions given in Part 1 of the 
standard, shall apply. 

3. TYPES OF PIPETTES 

3.1 Cjrraduated pipettes for which a waiting time of 15s is specified shall 
be of one type as indicated below: 

f^ 4 — Graduated pipettes adjusted for delivery of a liquid from 
zero line at the top to any graduation line, nominal capacity 
obtained by deliverv down to the jet, 158 waiting time specified 
for accuracy Class A only. 



^Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). 

tPA»tH>lM of construction and adjustment of volumetric glassware. 



IS:41d2(Pirt3).19a5 

4. ACCURACY 

4.1 The graduated pipettes shall have A Class of accuracy only and shall 
conform to the requirement of 4, Part 1 of this standard. 

5. NOMINAL CAPACITY 

5.1 The graduated pipettes shall be 0*5 ml, 1 ml, 2 ml, 5 ml, 10 ml and 
25 ml nominal capacities respectively. 

5.2 Procedure for Measurement of Capacity 

5.2.1 The procedure given in 5.2, Part 1 of this standard shall be 
followed. 

6. LIMITS OF VOLUMETRIC ERROR 

6.1 Errors in the delivered Volume of Class A graduated pipettes shall 
not exceed the limits shown in Table 1, Part 1 of this standard. 

7. CONSTRUCTION 

7.1 Material 

7.1.1 Graduated pipettes shall be constructed from glass of suitable 
chemical and thermal properties, shall be as far as possible free from 
visible defects and shall be reasonably free from internal stress. When 
graded according to the method prescribed in IS: 2303-1963* the pipettes 
shall conform to Type 1 of the glass. 

7«2 Dimensions — Graduated pipettes shall comply with the dimensional 
requirements given in Table 2, Part 1 of this standard. 

7.3 Finish, Top of Pipettes and Delivery Jet 

7.3.1 Graduated pipettes shall comply with the requirements given 
in 7.3, 73.1 and 7.3.2, Part 1 of this standard. 

8. GRADUATION AND FIGURING 

8.1 Graduated pattern 1 or 2 of 8.3.1 and 8.3.2, Part 1 of this standard, 
shall be applied and typical figuring of graduation shall be as shown in 
Fig. 1. 

8.2 Lowest graduation and lowest figured graduation lines shall be in 
accordance with Table 1. 

9. PERMANENCY AND VISIBILITY OF GRADUATION LINES, 
FIGURES INSCRIPTIONS AND MARKINGS 

9.1 Graduation pipettes shall comply with the requirements given in 9, 
Part 1 of this standard*

10. SETTING OF THE MENISCUS 

10.1 Setting of the meniscus shall be performed in accordance with 10, 
Part 1 of this standard. 

11. DELIVERY TIME 

11.1 When the delivery time is marked on the pipette, then the observed 
delivery time and the marked delivery time shall both be within the 
limits given in Table 2 and shall not differ by more than 2s.

12. COLOUR CODING 

12.1 Ifcolour coding is used on the graduated pipettes, it shall comply 
with the requirements of IS : 1 1468-198S* and IS : 1 l469-198St. 



specification for colour coding of pipettes.

IS : 4162 ( Part 3 ) - 1985 

13. MARKING AND PACKING 

13.1 Each pipettes shall be marked permanently and legibly on surface 
with the following information: 

a) Nominal capacity followed by 'ml'; 

b) Letter 2TC to indicate the reference temperature; 

c) Letter *A' to indicate the class of accuracy for which the pipette 
has been adjusted; 

d) Waiting time of 15s shall be indicated on the graduated pipettes; 

e) Delivery time; 

f ) Type of pipette; 

g) Letter 'Ex' to indicate that the pipette has been adjusted for 
delivery; and 

h) Maker's name or recognized trade-mark, if any. 

13.1.1 The pipette may also be marked with the ISI Certification 
Mark. 

Note — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of 
the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and 
Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on the products covered by an 
Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply 
with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated 
by the producer. ISI marked products and also continuously checked by ISI for 
conformity to that standard under as a further safeguard. Details of conditions 
under which a licence for the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufac* 
turer or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution. 

13.2 The pipettes shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and 
the supplier. 

14. SAMPLING 

14.1 Representative samples of the graduated pipettes shall be drawn as 
prescribed in Appendix C of Part 1 of this standard.
